quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The terms outlined in this contract ___ binding upon signature.
quests.completedSentence: The terms outlined in this contract are binding upon signature.
quests.grammarRule: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The terms' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Outlined in this contract' describes the terms - find the true plural subject.
quests.example: The terms outlined in this contract are binding upon signature.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither party ___ permitted to disclose confidential information.
quests.completedSentence: Neither party is permitted to disclose confidential information.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither' takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither party' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about how many parties 'neither party' refers to at a time.
quests.example: Neither party is permitted to disclose confidential information.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The attorney representing both defendants ___ requested an extension.
quests.completedSentence: The attorney representing both defendants has requested an extension.
quests.grammarRule: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The attorney' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Representing both defendants' describes the attorney - it doesn't change the subject's number.
quests.example: The attorney representing both defendants has requested an extension.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The samples collected from this experiment ___ still being analyzed.
quests.completedSentence: The samples collected from this experiment are still being analyzed.
quests.grammarRule: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The samples' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether 'samples' is one item or many before choosing the verb.
quests.example: The samples collected from this experiment are still being analyzed.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each variable in this study ___ carefully controlled.
quests.completedSentence: Each variable in this study is carefully controlled.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each variable' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider whether 'each' looks at the variables together or one at a time.
quests.example: Each variable in this study is carefully controlled.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The hypothesis proposed by the researchers ___ untested.
quests.completedSentence: The hypothesis proposed by the researchers remains untested.
quests.grammarRule: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The hypothesis' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify the head noun and set aside the phrase describing who proposed it.
quests.example: The hypothesis proposed by the researchers remains untested.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Appositive phrase does not change the number of the subject it renames
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The Amazon rainforest, home to millions of species, ___ nine countries.
quests.completedSentence: The Amazon rainforest, home to millions of species, spans nine countries.
quests.grammarRule: Appositive phrase does not change the number of the subject it renames
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The Amazon rainforest' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'spans'.
quests.nativeTip: The appositive between the commas describes the rainforest - it doesn't add a new subject.
quests.example: The Amazon rainforest, home to millions of species, spans nine countries.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Coral reefs around the world ___ increasingly vulnerable to rising ocean temperatures.
quests.completedSentence: Coral reefs around the world become increasingly vulnerable to rising ocean temperatures.
quests.grammarRule: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Coral reefs' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'become'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Coral reefs' is already plural - match the verb to that.
quests.example: Coral reefs around the world become increasingly vulnerable to rising ocean temperatures.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither volcanic activity nor tectonic shifts ___ fully understood by scientists yet.
quests.completedSentence: Neither volcanic activity nor tectonic shifts are fully understood by scientists yet.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'tectonic shifts', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the two nouns joined by 'nor' and see which one sits next to the verb.
quests.example: Neither volcanic activity nor tectonic shifts are fully understood by scientists yet.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Officials from the ministry ___ expected to announce new measures today.
quests.completedSentence: Officials from the ministry are expected to announce new measures today.
quests.grammarRule: Plural subject in the simple present
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Officials' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Find the subject and ask whether the phrase about the ministry alters it.
quests.example: Officials from the ministry are expected to announce new measures today.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The number of cases reported in this region ___ each week.
quests.completedSentence: The number of cases reported in this region rises each week.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The number of cases' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'rises'.
quests.nativeTip: Is this sentence about the cases themselves, or the count of them?
quests.example: The number of cases reported in this region rises each week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Residents living near the affected area ___ growing increasingly concerned.
quests.completedSentence: Residents living near the affected area are growing increasingly concerned.
quests.grammarRule: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Residents' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify the head noun - does the phrase about the affected area change it?
quests.example: Residents living near the affected area are growing increasingly concerned.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: "Hey, do you know if my brother and his roommate ___ coming to the barbecue?"
quests.completedSentence: "Hey, do you know if my brother and his roommate are coming to the barbecue?"
quests.grammarRule: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'My brother and his roommate' is a compound subject, so it's plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Two people joined by 'and' always form a plural subject, even in casual speech.
quests.example: "Hey, do you know if my brother and his roommate are coming to the barbecue?"

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: "Honestly, everyone at that party ___ having such a good time."
quests.completedSentence: "Honestly, everyone at that party is having such a good time."
quests.grammarRule: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Casual speech doesn't change the rules: how does 'everyone' behave?
quests.example: "Honestly, everyone at that party is having such a good time."

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: "I think either my sister or my cousins ___ bringing dessert tonight."
quests.completedSentence: "I think either my sister or my cousins are bringing dessert tonight."
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'my cousins', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: With 'either...or', check the noun closest to the verb.
quests.example: "I think either my sister or my cousins are bringing dessert tonight."

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Every purchase made this weekend ___ a free gift.
quests.completedSentence: Every purchase made this weekend includes a free gift.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Every purchase' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'includes'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider whether 'every' treats purchases together or one at a time.
quests.example: Every purchase made this weekend includes a free gift.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Our new collection, along with several limited-edition pieces, ___ available starting Monday.
quests.completedSentence: Our new collection, along with several limited-edition pieces, is available starting Monday.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'our new collection', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The limited-edition pieces mentioned after 'along with' don't add a second subject.
quests.example: Our new collection, along with several limited-edition pieces, is available starting Monday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Customers who sign up today ___ an exclusive discount.
quests.completedSentence: Customers who sign up today receive an exclusive discount.
quests.grammarRule: The main verb agrees with the main subject, not a distractor noun inside the relative clause
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Customers' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'receive'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify who 'who sign up today' describes, then find the main subject.
quests.example: Customers who sign up today receive an exclusive discount.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Percentage + 'of' + singular/uncountable noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Sixty percent of the company's revenue ___ from international sales.
quests.completedSentence: Sixty percent of the company's revenue comes from international sales.
quests.grammarRule: Percentage + 'of' + singular/uncountable noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Revenue' is treated as a singular, uncountable noun here, so 'sixty percent of the company's revenue' takes a singular verb: 'comes'.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether 'revenue' is countable like 'employees', or one whole amount.
quests.example: Sixty percent of the company's revenue comes from international sales.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Collective noun takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The board of directors ___ meeting to discuss its merger proposal.
quests.completedSentence: The board of directors is meeting to discuss its merger proposal.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The board of directors' is a singular collective noun, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'The board of directors' names one governing body, even though it has many members.
quests.example: The board of directors is meeting to discuss its merger proposal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the shareholders nor the CEO ___ satisfied with this quarter's results.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the shareholders nor the CEO is satisfied with this quarter's results.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the CEO', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Compare the two nouns after 'neither' and 'nor' - which one is next to the verb?
quests.example: Neither the shareholders nor the CEO is satisfied with this quarter's results.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The number of endangered species ___ every year.
quests.completedSentence: The number of endangered species grows every year.
quests.grammarRule: 'The number of' + plural noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The number of endangered species' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'grows'.
quests.nativeTip: Is this sentence about the species themselves, or the count of them?
quests.example: The number of endangered species grows every year.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each ecosystem in this region ___ its own delicate balance.
quests.completedSentence: Each ecosystem in this region has its own delicate balance.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each ecosystem' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider whether 'each' looks at ecosystems together or one at a time.
quests.example: Each ecosystem in this region has its own delicate balance.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Rising sea levels, along with extreme weather events, ___ coastal communities worldwide.
quests.completedSentence: Rising sea levels, along with extreme weather events, threaten coastal communities worldwide.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: The original subject is 'rising sea levels', which is plural. The verb stays in the base form: 'threaten'.
quests.nativeTip: The extreme weather events mentioned after 'along with' don't add a second subject.
quests.example: Rising sea levels, along with extreme weather events, threaten coastal communities worldwide.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The exhibit featuring works from several local artists ___ open through the end of the month.
quests.completedSentence: The exhibit featuring works from several local artists remains open through the end of the month.
quests.grammarRule: A long descriptive noun phrase still has one true head noun that determines agreement
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The exhibit' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: Identify the head noun and set aside the phrase describing what it features.
quests.example: The exhibit featuring works from several local artists remains open through the end of the month.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the sculptures nor the paintings ___ for sale at this gallery.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the sculptures nor the paintings are for sale at this gallery.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the paintings', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: In a 'neither...nor' pair, position matters - which noun is nearest the blank?
quests.example: Neither the sculptures nor the paintings are for sale at this gallery.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each performance in this festival ___ a different cultural tradition.
quests.completedSentence: Each performance in this festival celebrates a different cultural tradition.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each performance' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'celebrates'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider whether 'each' looks at performances together or one at a time.
quests.example: Each performance in this festival celebrates a different cultural tradition.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Collective noun takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The committee overseeing this merger ___ its decision by Friday.
quests.completedSentence: The committee overseeing this merger makes its decision by Friday.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun takes a singular verb when acting as one unit
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The committee' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Overseeing this merger' describes the committee - the subject stays a singular collective noun.
quests.example: The committee overseeing this merger makes its decision by Friday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the researchers nor the funding agency ___ ready to comment publicly.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the researchers nor the funding agency is ready to comment publicly.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the funding agency', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Check which of the two nouns joined by 'nor' comes last before the verb.
quests.example: Neither the researchers nor the funding agency is ready to comment publicly.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: A number of small businesses in this district ___ with the new regulations.
quests.completedSentence: A number of small businesses in this district struggle with the new regulations.
quests.grammarRule: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'A number of small businesses' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'struggle'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about what 'a number of' signals about the businesses: a single count, or several separate ones?
quests.example: A number of small businesses in this district struggle with the new regulations.
